summary: DeltaPulse is a web-based coastal monitoring and visualization platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to explore shoreline changes and environmental conditions in the Sundarbans. Built using React, Vite, JavaScript, MapLibre GL JS, and Recharts, it integrates satellite imagery, geographic information, and environmental datasets. The platform uses NASA GIBS (VIIRS NOAA-20), ASF DAAC (NISAR GCOV), Open-Meteo Marine and Weather APIs, Esri World Imagery, and CARTO. GeoJSON represents shoreline boundaries and geographic features, while raster and vector layers display satellite imagery and spatial data. Interactive maps, layer controls, location selection, coherence filtering, and time-series charts help users compare shoreline positions from 2015 to 2025 and explore coastal changes. Deployed through Cloudflare, DeltaPulse brings diverse data sources into one interface, making complex environmental information more accessible and easier to understand.
details:
DeltaPulse

Continuous Coastal Monitoring of the Sundarbans

DeltaPulse is a web-based coastal monitoring platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It lets users select a coastal area, with the Sundarbans as our focus, and continuously monitor shoreline change, land subsidence, wave height, sea-surface temperature, wind and precipitation. It is designed to record these changes and connect automatically with NASA’s NISAR data.

How It Works

Users see satellite imagery, shoreline boundaries and environmental data on one interactive map. They can toggle layers, filter by coherence, compare shorelines from 2015 to 2025, and view changes in charts.

Data Sources

NASA GIBS, ASF DAAC (NISAR GCOV products), Open-Meteo Marine and Weather APIs, Esri World Imagery and CARTO.

Impact

DeltaPulse brings scattered coastal data into one place, helping researchers, planners and local communities track erosion and subsidence in the Sundarbans and protect people and mangroves.

Tools

React, Vite, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, MapLibre GL JS, Recharts, GeoJSON, Python and Java, deployed on Cloudflare.

Creativity

It combines satellite and vector map layers with ocean and weather data in one interface, making complex NISAR radar data easy for non-experts to explore.

Factors Considered

Reliability, availability and update frequency of the data sources

Ease of use for non-technical users

The Sundarbans’ vulnerability to sea-level rise, erosion and storms

Automatic connection to NISAR data for continuous monitoring
